name: HOTEL YOSHI KAOHSIUNG
detail: The overall stay experience was very good, with a convenient location, spacious room, comfortable bathroom, stable hot water supply, and pleasing views. The in-room WiFi performed well, and the facilities were complete and well-maintained; the cleanliness was reassuring, and the staff provided friendly and attentive service. Overall, the quality of the accommodation is commensurate with the price, making it a recommended choice.

name: Hotel YAM LAGOM
detail: Last year, I stayed around Milyedo because it was convenient to travel, but this time I chose this area. An excellent choice. There's no mustiness typical of old buildings, the view from the higher floors is refreshing, and the subway isn't far, so I stayed very comfortably. The bed sheets are clean, and there's a cola and an electrolyte drink in the fridge. The staff is also friendly!

name: River Trees Hotel
detail: The room is clean and located next to the light rail around the city, close to convenience stores. The room is clean and offers free wine to drink during designated times. The room is spacious with a comfortable bed and has windows. There is a female staff member who can speak Thai very well. You can check in 24 hours a day. All the staff provide excellent service.

name: River inn Station
detail: Within walking distance from Beautiful Island Station. There is also a bus stop nearby, making it easy to go to Sanpho Shrine. The breakfast was delicious, and light snacks were also provided in the evening. The air conditioning worked well, the shower had good water pressure and temperature, the room was clean, access was good, and it was reassuring to have staff at the front desk even at late hours. The size of the room is probably acceptable for a solo traveler, but it might feel cramped for two people. I’ve seen comments from others regarding odors in the rooms. However, in the morning, I noticed a sewer smell coming up from the shower room, so I would recommend taking a shower in the evening. If you keep the bathroom door closed, the smell did not fill the bedroom. When I returned from being out at night, the smell had disappeared, so it was not unbearable.

name: Single Inn - Kaohsiung Station
detail: If you're looking for a private room with a space for one person rather than a guesthouse, and you don't mind shared toilets and showers, I think this is a good budget accommodation. It's close to Kaohsiung Station and a convenience store. When I checked in this time, they assisted me in Japanese. Upon going to the floor where my room was, there was a shoe box for each room, and I changed into slippers. I booked a single room, which has a very simple interior. The air conditioning is of a non-adjustable type. The walls are thin, and I could hear the sound of doors opening and closing, as well as noises from the hallway, but I’m not the type to mind that too much, so it was fine for me. On the second floor, there's a lounge area with large windows where you can overlook the city, and you can eat or have tea there. There’s also a free water dispenser. On the same floor, there are laundry facilities, a large bath, and toilets. A simple breakfast is included, with options like porridge, bread, salad, tea eggs, and drinks, which is appreciated. During breakfast, you inform the reception on the first floor of your room number, and they give you the utensils. At the end, you clean up your own dishes. It's also possible to walk to Liuhe Night Market, and the location is good, so I think I would like to stay here again.

name: Uno Backpackers Inn
detail: I stayed in a dormitory room. Although it was inexpensive, the bedding was clean and there were plenty of outlets. The partition curtains were a bit short, making it easy to come and go, and it was nice that I could quietly enter and exit even at night. The noise from the neighboring rooms was clearly audible, so earplugs are a must; there were no hangers inside the beds, and they were shared in the room. The kitchen was convenient to use and was always kept clean and tidy.

name: Ahiruyah Guest House
detail: This is my second time using it, and the location is excellent. From Kaohsiung Airport, take the MRT Red Line to the Formosa Boulevard Station, and it's in a building that has a 7-Eleven on the first floor. It's been open for a number of years, I suppose? You can feel some age in certain areas, such as the bed and curtains, among others. There are quite a few guests, but the lounge and restrooms are kept clean, and the cleaning is thorough. It's also a big plus that the staff can speak Japanese.

name: Jezreel Inn
detail: First of all, the accommodation is really clean and spacious. The bedding is also clean and nice. It seems like the staff manages everything very carefully! And there seem to be a male and a female owner, both of whom were really kind. When I was struggling to boil instant noodles, they helped me out... One thing I wish was different is that it would be great if there was air conditioning in the bathroom as well. In the summer, it feels a bit humid after showering, so having air conditioning in the bathroom would make it much more comfortable. Oh, and it's a good idea to bring your own water bottle! Otherwise, buy water or drinks and don't throw away the plastic bottles; rinse them and reuse them at the accommodation. Otherwise, you'll have to use the cups provided in the accommodation, which you'll need to wash each time, and they're small. It would be better to bring a water bottle and fill it at the water purifier! Also, you can eat freely in the common area. The entrance is slightly behind the restaurant, which can look a bit dirty, but once you get inside the accommodation, it’s very pleasant, so don’t worry too much. If you come out of exit 3 of the station, it’s right in front of you; don’t wander far, just enter through the entrance next to the café you see on the right. Anyway, if I get to visit Kaohsiung again, I would like to use this place again. I recommend it!

name: DreamWell Hostel
detail: Positive points: - It’s only one train ride (20 minutes, 25 Taiwan dollars) from Kaohsiung Airport, and it takes about an 8-minute walk straight from the station to get there. - You can always drink delicious coffee from the coffee machine. - Free breakfast (toast and three types of jam; the coconut jam was delicious). - After a long trip, I was allowed early check-in just before I almost collapsed during transit. - There were curtains installed on the beds. - The toilet and shower were clean. Shampoo and body soap were provided. - No issues with wifi. - The staff were young and provided assistance in English and Japanese. Points to note: - Before check-in, you need to ring the bell at the entrance to have the door unlocked, but you couldn't enter until after 10 AM even if you rang the bell. After check-in, you unlock it with a card key. - No towels provided.

name: Idol Hotel
detail: First of all, I booked a cost-effective accommodation. I’m not planning to stay in Kaohsiung the whole time; I intend to go around and sleep wherever I like, so I chose a place at an affordable price. I had seen reviews saying it lacks soundproofing, and that is true; you can have a conversation with the neighboring rooms. However, for people who fall asleep as soon as they lie down, it doesn't matter. It's located between stations, but if you walk a bit, there are many good restaurants and fruit shops, which is nice. There are many local breakfast spots in the alley. The air conditioning can be turned on and off. The blankets are a bit thin, but the water pressure is good, and hot water comes out well. On the first day, they only provided two bottles of water and didn’t give more, so I had to buy some. There’s no deposit. Just a short walk from the accommodation, there’s a night market, and in front, there are streetlights and a mini park, which is great for experiencing the ambiance of Taiwan. If I visit again for a longer stay, I would be willing to stay here again.
